title: Construction of a Human Aorta Smooth Muscle Cell Organ-On-A-Chip Model for Recapitulating Biomechanical Strain in the Aortic Wall
protocol: Wash the right lateral region of the ascending aorta with sterile PBS.
Remove the intima and adventitia layers of the tissue using two ophthalmic forceps.
Retain the media layer to harvest the cells.
Place the media layer onto a 10 cm culture dish.
Cut the media layer into small pieces (2-3 mm) with scissors.
Add 5 mL of smooth muscle cell culture medium (SMCM) containing 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin to the culture dish.
Move the tissue pieces into a culture bottle using a sterile dropper, spreading them evenly.
Discard as much of the initial culture medium as possible.
Invert the culture bottle upside down.
Add 2 mL of SMCM to the inverted culture bottle and place it in an incubator (5% CO2) at 37 °C for 1-2 hours.
Slowly turn the culture bottle right side up after 1-2 hours.
Add another 2 mL of SMCM to the culture bottle.
Exchange the SMCM with fresh medium every 5-7 days.
Incubate for approximately 2 weeks until sporadic smooth muscle cells climb out.
Slowly discard the SMCM and add it slowly when changing the medium.
Transport the culture bottle slowly when moving to a microscope station.
Wash cells with 2 mL of PBS when they reach approximately 80% confluency.
Digest cells with 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin.
Divide digested cells into two new culture bottles with 4 mL of fresh SMCM.
Identify cells through an immunofluorescence analysis of four different specific markers for smooth muscle cells (CNN1, SM22).
Add curing agent to base at a weight ratio of A: B = 10:1 w/w for PDMS polymerization.
Mix the complex completely for 5 min.
Place the prepared PDMS gel in a vacuum extraction tank for 30-60 min.
Maintain pressure below -0.8 mPa during extraction.
Design mold with a 100 mm × 40 mm × 8 mm external frame structure and a 70 mm × 6 mm × 4 mm channel using CAD software.
Custom make the molds of three layers using a high-precision computer numerical control engraving machine.
Carve out the frame of the molds and the microchannels using PMMA plates.
Glue carved PMMA plates onto another PMMA plate.
Pour PDMS gel onto a mold with dimensions 100 mm × 40 mm × 6 mm and a channel of 70 mm × 6 mm × 4 mm.
Cross-link the poured PDMS gel at 70 °C for 1-2 hours.
Peel off cross-linked PDMS slabs from the mold.
Cut commercialized PDMS membranes into sections measuring 100 mm × 40 mm.
Treat three prepared PDMS slabs and two PDMS membranes with oxygen plasma for 5 minutes.
Punch holes on the three PDMS slabs using a 1 mm hole puncher to create inlet and outlet microchannels.

Bond three PDMS slabs and two PDMS membranes together in the order: air channel PDMS slab (top layer) - PDMS membrane - medium channel PDMS slab (middle layer) - PDMS membrane - air channel PDMS slab (bottom layer).
Insert a 1 mm outer diameter and 1 cm long stainless-steel needle into one end of a prepared hose.
Insert a Luer into the other end of the hose to create tubes connected to the air and medium microchannels of the PDMS chip.
Insert the prepared tubes into the outlets and inlets of the air and medium microchannels on the PDMS chip.
Infuse 2 mL of 80 mg/mL mouse collagen into the medium microchannel of the PDMS chip using a 2 mL syringe.
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Remove the collagen from the channel and recollect with a 2 mL syringe.
Place the collagen-coated PDMS chips in a 60 °C incubator overnight.
Place the PDMS chips in a UV sterilizer for more than 1 h.
Place the sterilized PDMS chips on an ultraclean bench in preparation for the cell experiment.

Culture 4 x 10^5 primary human smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) from patients using smooth muscle cell medium (SMCM) containing 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin in an 5% CO2 incubator at 37 °C.
Discard the SMCM when the HASMC density reaches 80%.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of PBS.
Digest the cells using 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin for 2 min.
Centrifuge at 100 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of fresh SMCM.
Use 8 mL of SMCM to culture the cells on a 10 cm culture dish.
Calculate the cell number using a cytometer.
Use the cells at a final concentration of 2 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Slowly pour 2 mL of PBS into the collagen-coated and sterilized PDMS chip medium microchannel.
Discard using a 2 mL syringe.
Slowly pour 2 mL of 2 x 10^5 cells/mL HASMC suspension into the medium microchannel of the PDMS chip using a 2 mL syringe.
Close the Luer at the entrance and exit of the PDMS chip.
Place the PDMS chip in an incubator (5% CO2) at 37°C for 1 day.
Connect the outlet of the air microchannel on the PDMS chip to the vacuum controller system when cells are attached after 24 hours.
Turn on the solenoid valve and the vacuum pump.
Adjust the pressure level to 10 kPa for 7.18 ± 0.44% strain and 15 kPa for 17.28 ± 0.91% strain.
Place the PDMS chips in an incubator (5% CO2) at 37°C and stretch for 24 hours.
Prepare several solenoid valves, vacuum filters, vacuum regulators, a vacuum pump, a peristaltic pump, and a programmable logic controller (PLC).
Program the PLC controller and set the on/off time interval to 1 Hz.
Connect the solenoid valves to the programmed controller.
Connect the inlet of the vacuum pump to the vacuum filters.
Connect the outlet of the vacuum filters to the vacuum regulators.
Connect the outlet of the vacuum regulators to solenoid valves.
Connect the outlet of the solenoid valves to the outlets of the air microchannels of the PDMS chips.
Connect the outlet of the peristaltic pump to the inlet of the medium microchannel of the PDMS chip.
Connect the inlet of the peristaltic pump to the outlet of the medium microchannel PDMS chip.
Adjust the amplitude of the strain by the regulator.
Adjust the strain frequency by the microcontroller.
